caption: The online shopping came to R1 300 and I would have sworn it was R500. Is your clothing account this bad too?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R15 500
p/m salary
Living in Springs
slides.body:
Female, 23
Single, shares a 2 bed flat with a varsity friend
Job: Junior graphic designer
Net salary: R15 500 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Half of a 2 bed in Springs, water, refuse
slides.body: It's the only way either of us could afford somewhere close to the office. I still put my headphones on the second I get home.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, plus the days I forget lunch and buy it at work
slides.body: I cook properly maybe twice a week. The rest is whatever's fastest.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi most days, Uber when I'm running late
slides.body: No car yet. Some months this line costs nearly as much as rent.

slides.title: Clothing account & online shopping
slides.includes: Mr Price account, plus the online carts I don't remember filling
slides.body: I told myself it was maybe R500. It's R1 300. I don't fully know where the rest went.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: Airtime for my gran, extra when my mom's short
slides.body: It's not a lot, but it's the one debit order I've never once questioned.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, phone & data, funeral policy, a stokvel with two friends from res, savings, a gym I go to twice a month
slides.body: Six small things I'd never added up before this. Together they're more than my rent.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R15 500. That's about R23 a day until payday, and this is only my second year earning a proper salary.

slides.title: I stopped guessing where it went
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The online shopping alone came to R1 300 — I would have guessed R500.

No bank login needed.
